numerical_failure.expected_behavior: Avoid illegal conversion/undefined behavior when `n` is not a valid integer; for NaN inputs, do not convert `n` to an integer type for the `eval_gegenbauer_l` branch.
trigger_conditions: `scipy.special.orthogonal_eval.eval_gegenbauer` is called with `n` containing an invalid value like `nan` (UBSAN reported illegal conversion of `n` to an integer)
oracle_clues: PR#25690: “fix UBSAN crash for NaN” in `orthogonal_eval.pxd` for `special.eval_gegenbauer`.
PR#25690: UBSAN revealed “illegal conversion of `n` to an integer when it may contain an invalid value like `nan`.”

The change sidesteps UB by gating the integer fast-path: old code cast `n` to `long long` (`ni = <long long> n`) and then used the integer path if `number_t is double and n == ni and n < 1e10`; new code only calls `eval_gegenbauer_l` when `number_t is double and n >= 0 and n < 1e10 and n == <long long> n` and performs the `Py_ssize_t` conversion on `<long long> n` rather than via an intermediate value.

The diff specifically shows the conditional guard added: `n >= 0 and n < 1e10 and n == <long long> n` before calling `eval_gegenbauer_l(<Py_ssize_t> n, ...)` (with `Py_ssize_t` sourced from the `n == <long long> n`-validated integer form).

numerical_characteristics.magnitude: n < 1e10 (and n >= 0) for the integer-fast-path check
category_specific_evidence: The bug is annotated as a special value bug: PR#25690 says “fix UBSAN crash for NaN” in eval_gegenbauer and that `n` may contain “invalid value like `nan`”.
PR#25690/orthogonal_eval.pxd show the illegal conversion involved is “illegal conversion of `n` to an integer” when `n` may be `nan`.

The code change avoids converting `n` to an integer via an intermediate cast; it now only calls `eval_gegenbauer_l` when `number_t is double and n >= 0 and n < 1e10 and n == <long long> n` (i.e., the integer fast-path is gated, preventing the NaN case).
The test update adds NaN coverage for Gegenbauer: `@pytest.mark.parametrize('n', [0, 1, 2, 3.2, np.nan])` and also tests NaN for `alpha` (`alpha` includes `np.nan`) and `x` (`x` includes `np.nan`).
reproduction_risks: Reproduction may need UBSAN/undefined-behavior tooling to observe the crash caused by illegal conversion of `n` when `n` is NaN.

The fast-path is only taken under specific conditions (`number_t is double`, `n >= 0`, `n < 1e10`, and `n == <long long> n`); using NaN must ensure the old/unsafe conversion path was reachable before the fix.
Because only the NaN case is explicitly evidenced, reproductions involving other special values (±inf, signed zero, subnormals) may not match the reported bug.
